cards.front: conductor
cards.back: A material that lets heat or electricity pass through easily.
cards.say: conductor. A material that lets heat or electricity pass through easily.

cards.front: insulator
cards.back: A material that does not let heat or electricity pass through easily.
cards.say: insulator. A material that does not let heat or electricity pass through easily.

cards.front: electrical conductor
cards.back: A material that lets electricity flow through it. Most metals are electrical conductors.
cards.say: electrical conductor. A material that lets electricity flow through it. Most metals are electrical conductors.

cards.front: electrical insulator
cards.back: A material that does not let electricity flow through. Plastic, rubber and wood are electrical insulators.
cards.say: electrical insulator. A material that does not let electricity flow through. Plastic, rubber and wood are electrical insulators.

cards.front: thermal conductor
cards.back: A material that lets heat move through it easily. Metals are thermal conductors.
cards.say: thermal conductor. A material that lets heat move through it easily. Metals are thermal conductors.

cards.front: thermal insulator
cards.back: A material that slows down heat. Wool and foam are thermal insulators.
cards.say: thermal insulator. A material that slows down heat. Wool and foam are thermal insulators.

cards.front: Is copper an electrical conductor?
cards.back: Yes.
cards.say: Is copper an electrical conductor? Yes.

cards.front: Is rubber an electrical conductor?
cards.back: No. Rubber is an insulator.
cards.say: Is rubber an electrical conductor? No. Rubber is an insulator.

cards.front: Is plastic a conductor of electricity?
cards.back: No. It is an insulator.
cards.say: Is plastic a conductor of electricity? No. It is an insulator.

cards.front: Is steel a good conductor of heat?
cards.back: Yes.
cards.say: Is steel a good conductor of heat? Yes.

cards.front: Why are saucepans made of metal?
cards.back: Metal is a thermal conductor, so heat passes quickly to the food.
cards.say: Why are saucepans made of metal? Metal is a thermal conductor, so heat passes quickly to the food.

cards.front: Why are saucepan handles made of plastic or wood?
cards.back: They are thermal insulators, so your hand stays safe.
cards.say: Why are saucepan handles made of plastic or wood? They are thermal insulators, so your hand stays safe.

cards.front: Why are electrical wires covered in plastic?
cards.back: Plastic is an insulator, so it keeps the electricity safe inside.
cards.say: Why are electrical wires covered in plastic? Plastic is an insulator, so it keeps the electricity safe inside.

cards.front: Why is the metal part of a wire in the middle?
cards.back: Metal is a conductor, so the electricity can flow through it.
cards.say: Why is the metal part of a wire in the middle? Metal is a conductor, so the electricity can flow through it.

cards.front: Why do we wear gloves in cold weather?
cards.back: Wool is a thermal insulator and keeps heat in.
cards.say: Why do we wear gloves in cold weather? Wool is a thermal insulator and keeps heat in.

cards.front: Why does a metal spoon feel cold?
cards.back: Metal conducts heat away from your hand quickly.
cards.say: Why does a metal spoon feel cold? Metal conducts heat away from your hand quickly.

cards.front: Why does a wooden spoon feel less cold?
cards.back: Wood is an insulator, so it does not take heat from your hand so fast.
cards.say: Why does a wooden spoon feel less cold? Wood is an insulator, so it does not take heat from your hand so fast.

cards.front: Which keeps a drink hot longer, a foam cup or a metal cup?
cards.back: A foam cup, because foam is an insulator.
cards.say: Which keeps a drink hot longer, a foam cup or a metal cup? A foam cup, because foam is an insulator.

cards.front: Is aluminium foil a conductor?
cards.back: Yes, of heat and electricity.
cards.say: Is aluminium foil a conductor? Yes, of heat and electricity.

cards.front: Is glass a good conductor of electricity?
cards.back: No. Glass is an insulator.
cards.say: Is glass a good conductor of electricity? No. Glass is an insulator.

cards.front: Is graphite (pencil lead) a conductor?
cards.back: Yes. It is a non-metal that conducts electricity.
cards.say: Is graphite (pencil lead) a conductor? Yes. It is a non-metal that conducts electricity.

cards.front: How can you test if a material conducts electricity?
cards.back: Put it into a circuit with a bulb. If the bulb lights, it conducts.
cards.say: How can you test if a material conducts electricity? Put it into a circuit with a bulb. If the bulb lights, it conducts.

cards.front: Which are better conductors of electricity, metals or non-metals?
cards.back: Metals, mostly.
cards.say: Which are better conductors of electricity, metals or non-metals? Metals, mostly.

cards.front: True or false: An insulator stops heat and electricity moving easily.
cards.back: True.
cards.say: True or false: An insulator stops heat and electricity moving easily. True.

cards.front: Why is a plug made of plastic outside?
cards.back: Plastic is an insulator so you do not get a shock.
cards.say: Why is a plug made of plastic outside? Plastic is an insulator so you do not get a shock.
